articles.title: AI investments stress the stock market
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
It was generally up yesterday on the world's stock exchanges, but post-market trading was characterized by the market's increased focus on technology companies' investments, or rather how earnings development relates to an expected cost increase for capex (a direct side effect of the autumn's rise in interest rates). While Meta was trading up, Tesla fell back. This morning, it is the same theme in Asia with falling prices for technology companies that are sinking the Kospi (at the time of writing, -2.6%). Stock market futures point to declines in both Europe and the US today. The USD strengthened slightly after a couple of weaker days and is at 1.12 against the EUR. There were relatively small movements in the fixed income market yesterday, but the fact that the French 10-year government bond yield rose above 5% gained attraction. The yield is now the highest since 2002, and rate spread versus its German counterpart is now close to 160 basis points, the largest difference in 15 years.
Oil prices up on continued unrest.
 The US is recalling non-essential personnel and relatives from Saudi Arabia after the recent Houthi attacks. Brent crude is rising this morning and is slightly above USD 110 per barrel. For the latest update of the large image package "Iran War Chartpack" click 
here
.
Today's statistical calendar
 offers business tendency survey from Norway and France. In addition, we get the last ECB figures before they enter a quiet period ahead of upcoming interest rate announcements. The reporting season continues with a number of large companies in Sweden.
Among other things, SEB reports an operating profit of SEK 9,412 million for Q3 (expected 9,936). SEB also reports that the share buy-back programme is paused, read more 
here
. 
Reading tips from SEB: 
1) 
ECB Preview
 – 
The ECB will keep interest rates unchanged next week before raising its policy rate in December. Continued risks linked to war and energy speak in favour of higher interest rates, but the rise in long-term interest rates is counteracting.
 2
) Investment Outlook update
–
yesterday raised the weight of government bonds from underweight to neutral and reduced the proportion of cash and investment grade bonds. Reduced risk of further long-term interest rate rises and the fact that the recent interest rate rise in itself provides a more attractive ongoing return and diversification are the reasons.
Nordic key stories
Margins and SEK lower Swedish petrol prices.
 When I wrote Nordic Alert last week, the price of petrol was around SEK 19.50 per litre. Since then, the price of crude oil has continued to rise, but the refining margins have been reduced significantly, which is now visible in the fact that the price of petrol is quoted around SEK 17.50. The appreciation of the krona in October may have contributed roughly 10 öre of the decline
Norwegian Business Tendency Survey for Q3.
 Manufacturing sentiment improved somewhat in Q2, pointing to modest production growth despite a continued decline in new orders. Demand was seen as an increasingly main constraint on further production growth. 
Other manufacturing sentiment surveys point to a broadly stable Business Tendency Survey in Q3.

articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Det var generellt uppåt igår på världens börser, men efterhandeln präglades av marknadens ökade fokus på teknikbolagens investeringar, eller rättare sagt hur vinstutvecklingen förhåller sig till en väntad kostnadsuppgång för de stora investeringar som görs (en direkt bieffekt av höstens ränteuppgång). Medan Meta handlades upp, föll Tesla tillbaka. Nu på morgonen är det samma tema i Asien med fallande kurser för teknikbolag som bland annat sänker Kospi (skrivande stund -2,6%). Börsterminer pekar mot nedgångar både i Europa och USA idag. USD stärktes något efter ett par svagare dagar och ligger på 1,12 mot EUR. Det var förhållandevis små rörelser på räntemarknaden igår, men att den franska 10-åriga statsobligationsräntan steg över 5% fick så klart uppmärksamhet. Räntan är nu den högsta sedan 2002, och skillnaden mot dess tyska motsvarighet ligger nu nära 160 räntepunkter, den största skillnaden på 15 år. Även om kommande omröstning om budget godkänns är det uppenbart att marknaden hyser låg tilltro till franska offentliga finanser och politiken i stort.
Oljepriser upp på fortsatta oroligheter.

articles.title: Wait-and-see, balancing inflation risks against market developments
articles.heading: ECB Preview
articles.fulltext:
We expect the ECB to leave its key policy rates unchanged at the 29 October meeting. Although energy prices appear to lie between the levels assumed in September’s adverse and severe scenarios, the recent surge in bond yields has attracted increasing attention from Governing Council members. Their communication supports our view—and current market expectations—that the next rate hike will come in December.
Key points
Interim checkpoint: 
The 
October
 meeting
 offers an opportunity to assess incoming data, with major policy decisions likely to 
remain
 on hold until 
the
 updated staff projections
 are published in December
Energy prices versus market tightening: 
High 
oil
 and 
gas
 prices point towards the adverse scenarios, but the sharp rise in global long-term bond yields is 
already 
doing much of the ECB’s tightening
Rates on hold: 
We maintain our forecast of 25bp rate hikes in December and March.
The ECB’s meeting on 29 October will serve as an interim checkpoint between the September and December rounds of macroeconomic projections. In recent years, including the two most recent rate hikes in June and September 2026, the ECB has preferred to make major policy decisions alongside more in-depth analysis, including updated staff projections and scenarios. The intervening meetings have served as checkpoints for assessing incoming data, evaluating how risks have evolved and identifying emerging risks.
Against this background, we highlight and comment on the latest developments below:
1.
Inflation outcomes
 have been broadly in line with projections. Goods inflation continues to edge higher, while services inflation is gradually easing or perhaps levelling off. Energy prices remain the main driver of inflation, with an increase spreading from fuel to household energy. There are few, if any, signs of indirect or second-round effects from high energy prices.
2.
Real economic activity
 continues to 
show
 clear 
signs of 
improvement. This is 
most evident
 in survey data, with confidence rising in both manufacturing and 
services
 despite 
the prospect of 
energy prices 
remaining
 higher for longer. 
Consumer
 confidence has improved since the beginning of 2026 but
 remains
 weak by historic metrics.
3.
Energy prices
—
and the 
conflict in the 
Middle East itself
—
remain key. 
Crude 
oil and, in particular, natural gas prices are significantly above the levels assumed in the ECB’s 
September 
baseline scenario
, which had a 
cut-off date
 of
 19 August
.
 Oil and natural gas prices are currently just above the levels 
assumed 
in the adverse scenario. However, futures 
prices suggest
 that natural gas will track the severe scenario more closely from 2027 onwards. High natural gas prices have also clearly pushed up electricity prices. Overall, energy prices look set to remain higher for longer.
4.
Financial conditions
 have tightened substantially, marking the most significant change since the September monetary policy meeting. Expectations for higher policy rates and, above all, the sharp rise in global long-term bond yields should weigh on economic activity with a lag. To some extent, this is a circular argument, as part of the rise in yields reflects expectations of higher central bank policy rates. Nevertheless, markets have 
already 
done some of the ECB’s heavy lifting, making the final rate hike less certain. This 
creates
 a new downside risk to the policy
-
rate path, a point highlighted by a growing number of Governing Council members in recent weeks.
ECB rhetoric and assessment
Recent ECB speeches emphasise that elevated energy prices have so far had no major spillover effects on other prices or, more importantly, on the expectations that shape wage-setting. There also appears to be broad agreement that further rate hikes are likely to be needed to address inflation risks and range of possible outcomes outlined in the latest staff projections. The overall impression is that there is no urgent need to act, allowing most policymakers to wait for the more comprehensive analysis in December. At the same time, they stress that the ECB stands ready to deliver additional hikes if necessary. The tightening of financial conditions in recent weeks has also attracted increasing attention.
Future leadership line-up
Alongside monetary policy, the ECB’s future leadership has attracted growing attention, as the terms of three key members—Lagarde, Lane and Schnabel—are due to expire in 2027. Isabel Schnabel is set to leave the ECB on 3 January. Rumours persist that President Lagarde could leave early either to lead the World Economic Forum or to enter the French presidential race. The time for resolving these uncertainties is drawing closer. Given the ECB’s close institutional ties with other EU bodies, the appointment of a new president would probably form part of a broader political package involving other European leadership roles. 
Economic developments and the inflation outlook 
will 
remain decisive, but the composition of the Governing Council can influence how the ECB interprets and responds
 to developments
, with implications 
that extend 
beyond communication alone.

articles.title: Krona gains ground - tonight’s earnings in focus
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
Market moves were generally modest yesterday in the absence of major economic data and earnings releases. European equities mostly declined, weighed down by the energy sector and unrest and debt concerns in France. US markets fared somewhat better, with the S&P 500 gaining 0.3% and the Nasdaq broadly unchanged. Asian markets are also more positive this morning, supported by a relatively strong start to the earnings season, while equity futures point to higher opens in both Europe and the US today. 
Reuters reports that 13% of S&P 500 companies have reported so far, of which 86% have beaten earnings forecasts. 
Meta and Tesla report after the US market closes tonight, potentially providing a stronger catalyst for markets.
The rise in French bond yields paused yesterday, while yields elsewhere were broadly unchanged. 
However, expectations of a Fed rate hike next week eased a little further, following weak September figures for home sales and construction activity. 
The dollar weakened against all other G10 currencies, although moves were generally modest, extending October’s consolidation after its strong gains in September.
Brent crude is trading close to USD 110 per barrel again, having briefly fallen yesterday on reports of renewed peace talks that were subsequently denied.
Today’s economic calendar
 is light, with UK inflation the main release of note (see below), alongside a few speeches by ECB and BoE officials that could provide insights ahead of their upcoming policymeetings. The main international focus, however, will be on tonight’s earnings releases from Meta and Tesla. Yesterday’s most important release, German PPI, showed a further rise as expected, driven by high energy prices.
Trump today: Diesel measures and peace efforts. 
The Trump administration has announced USD 8 billion in fuel subsidies for farmers struggling with rising diesel prices as the US harvest peaks and the midterm elections approach. 
Trump’s repeated efforts to bring down diesel prices recently suggest concern ahead of the elections. He is also pushing for an end to the war in Ukraine, with US envoy Steve Witkoff due to meet Putin today.
Alberta remains in Canada.
 According to unofficial results from Elections Alberta, an overwhelming majority of 76% voted against a proposal to begin a process towards independence in Monday’s referendum.
UK: Inflation and pre-budget speculation
. September inflation figures are due today. 
Both headline and core CPI inflation are expected to edge higher, supporting our own and market expectations of a Bank of England rate hike at its next meeting on 5 November. The UK will also present its budget next week. As in France, the government needs to address high public debt and a large budget deficit without upsetting either voters or financial markets too much. Budget speculation is therefore likely to intensify during the week. The Financial Times has already reported that Chancellor Healey will not raise capital gains tax and that the Treasury is expected to examine the economic benefits of bringing the UK closer to the EU again.
Nordic key stories
October brings a tailwind for the krona.
 Following an almost uninterrupted rise in EUR/SEK during August and September, the pair has turned lower in October. 
We have highlighted in several reports that the current market environment primarily favours carry strategies in FX, which involve buying high-yielding currencies and selling low-yielding ones. This creates a headwind for the krona. 
The effect has been particularly pronounced this autumn, as the yen, which is also typically used as a funding currency in these strategies, has been used less extensively because of FX intervention. More recently, market expectations of rate hikes by the Fed and other central banks have eased somewhat, weakening the dollar against most G10 currencies, including the krona. The krona is also benefiting from euro weakness in the wake of France’s problems, making the decline in EUR/SEK more pronounced. For a sustained strengthening of the krona, however, more central banks abroad need to move towards policy normalisation rather than further rate hikes—or, at the very least, markets need to increasingly anticipate and price in such a shift. 
That will probably require a more persistent disinflationary contribution from energy prices.
Favourable conditions for Swedish wage growth.
 The National Institute of Economic Research assesses the conditions ahead of the upcoming wage bargaining round in its Wage Formation Report. 
According to Swedish Radio, the institute concludes that higher corporate productivity provides favourable conditions for real wage growth over the next few years. The report will be published at 09:00 today.

articles.title: Kronan i medvind – kvällens rapporter i fokus
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Det var överlag små rörelser under gårdagen i avsaknad av viktiga makroekonomiska data och resultatrapporter. I Europa sjönk börserna generellt tyngda av energi och franska oroligheter/skuldproblem medan det var något mer positivt i USA med S&P 500 upp 0,3% och Nasdaq runt nollan. I Asien är tongångarna under morgonen också mer positiva med stöd av en relativt bra start på rapportsäsongen och börsterminerna pekar också på positiva öppningar i både Europa och USA idag. Bland annat Reuters rapporterar att av de 13% av S&P 500 företag som hitintills har rapporterat så har 86% har överträffat vinstprognoserna. Efter att de amerikanska börserna stängt ikväll så rapporterar Meta och Tesla vilket kan komma att sätta än större avtryck på marknaderna. 
De franska ränteuppgångarna pausades något under gårdagen och generellt var räntor förhållandevis oförändrade igår. Förväntningarna på en räntehöjning från Fed nästa vecka avtog dock ytterligare något efter svaga siffror för bostadsförsäljningen och byggverksamheten i september. Dollarn försvagades mot alla övriga G10 valutor även om rörelserna generellt inte var stora och fortsatte därmed den konsolidering vi sett i oktober efter att ha gått väldigt starkt under september. 
Brentoljan handlas återigen nära 110 dollar per fat, efter att tillfälligt under gårdagen ha fallit på uppgifter om förnyade fredsförhandlingar som senare dementerades. 
Dagens agenda
 är tunn, där endast inflation från Storbritannien sticker ut (mer nedan) och så lite tal från ECB och BOE som kan vara intressanta inför kommande räntemöten. Internationellt fokus ligger dock på ovan nämnda resultatrapporter från Meta och Tesla till kvällen. Gårdagens viktigaste siffra, tysk PPI, fortsatte som förväntat högre driven av höga energipriser.
Dagens Trump: Dieselåtgärder och fredsmäkleri.
 Trumpadministrationen har aviserat bränslebidrag på 8 miljarder dollar till jordbrukare som brottas med stigande dieselpriser samtidigt som skörden i USA når sin höjdpunkt och mellanårsvalet närmar sig. Trumps många försök att få ned dieselpriserna den senaste tiden tyder på oro inför valet. Han driver också på för ett slut på kriget i Ukraina där det senaste är det amerikanska sändebudet Steve Witkoff idag ska träffa Putin.
Alberta kvar i Kanada.
 Enligt inofficiella resultat från Elections Alberta röstade en överväldigande majoritet på 76% i måndagens folkomröstning nej till förslaget att inleda en process mot självständighet.
Storbritannien: Inflation och spekulationer inför budgeten.
 I dag publiceras inflationssiffror för september. Både KPI- och kärninflationen väntas stiga något och därmed ge stöd åt våra och marknadens förväntningar om en räntehöjning från Bank of England vid nästa räntemöte den 5 november. Nästa vecka är det också Storbritanniens tur att presentera en budget. Precis som i Frankrike behöver regeringen hantera en stor statsskuld och ett stort budgetunderskott utan att vare sig väljare eller finansmarknader blir alltför missnöjda. Spekulationerna inför budgeten lär därför tillta under veckan. Financial Times har redan rapporterat att finansminister Healey inte kommer att höja kapitalvinstskatten och att finansdepartementet väntas undersöka de ekonomiska fördelarna med att åter föra Storbritannien närmare EU.
Sverige
Kronan med medvind i oktober.
 Efter mer eller mindre oavbrutna uppgångar i EUR/SEK under augusti och september har valutaparet vänt ned i oktober. Vi har i flera rapporter betonat att marknadsmiljön just nu framför allt gynnar så kallade carrystrategier på valutamarknaden, där man köper valutor med hög ränta och säljer valutor med låg ränta. Det innebär motvind för kronan. Under hösten har denna faktor varit extra negativ, eftersom yenen, som vanligtvis också används som finansieringsvaluta i dessa strategier, har använts i mindre utsträckning till följd av valutainterventioner. Den senaste tiden har marknadens förväntningar på räntehöjningar från Fed och andra centralbanker dämpats något, vilket har fått dollarn att försvagas mot de flesta G10-valutor, däribland kronan. Kronan får dessutom stöd av att euron handlas svagt i kölvattnet av problemen i Frankrike, vilket gör nedgången i EUR/SEK ännu tydligare. För en varaktigt starkare krona behöver dock fler centralbanker i omvärlden gå mot en normalisering snarare än höjningar av styrräntorna – eller åtminstone behöver marknaden i större utsträckning börja förvänta sig och prisa in en sådan utveckling. För det krävs sannolikt att energipriserna ger ett mer ihållande bidrag till lägre inflation.
Bra läge för löneökningar.
 Konjunkturinstitutet analyserar förutsättningarna inför avtalsrörelsen i sin lönebildningsrapport. Enligt SR bedömer institutet att företagens ökade produktivitet ger goda förutsättningar för reallöneökningar de närmaste åren. Rapporten publiceras kl. 09.00 i dag.

articles.title: NOK 2bn in NST480 and NST490
articles.heading: NGB Spotlight
articles.fulltext:
On Wednesday Oct 21st, Norges Bank will hold a multiple tap auction where a total of NOK 2bn will be issued, split between the NST480 (2.00%, 04/2028) and the NST490 (4.125%, 06/2036) bonds. NST480 currently trades with a yield of 4.815%, implying a maturity-matched spread vs. Germany of 177bps and an ASW spread of -38.5bps. NST490 trades with a yield of 4.54%, with corresponding spread levels at 97bps and -11bps. The auction closes at 11.00 CET, and results will be available on Norges Bank’s website at 11.05 CET. 
On Wednesday, Norges Bank will auction a total of NOK 2bn split between NST480 (04/2028) and the new NST490 (06/2036) bonds. Both bonds were included in last week’s tap auction which performed strongly. Hence, we are not surprised that Norges Bank chooses to issue the same bonds in the upcoming auction, and with the total volume capped at NOK 2bn we expect the auction to run smoothly. In the previous 6 tap auctions including NST480, the bond has received an average bid-to-cover of 4.86 with an allotment share of 53%. Corresponding numbers for the 10 auctions in NST490 are 3.50 and 58%.
The past month has been brutal for global bond markets, with challenging market conditions and high volatility. NSTs have followed the trend abroad, with long yields having corrected somewhat lower from the peak in early October. This has helped to stabilize spreads vs. German equivalents, while NST ASW spreads continue to move largely sideways with lurking sellers in the mid-segment of the curve still around. Meanwhile, outright levels continue to attract demand.
Expectations for Norges Bank have increased somewhat recently with the market discounting a 60% probability for another rate hike by December 2026 and a policy rate peak at 4.73% by March 2027. We reiterate our forecast that the policy rate peak has been reached and that normalization of the policy rate can begin by fall of next year. Our inflation forecast is higher than Norges Bank’s Sep near-term forecast, but we predict slightly lower core inflation in 2027.
Supply update: Following this auction, Norges Bank has issued a total of NOK 99bn YTD, while the annual borrowing interval is set at NOK 100-110bn (107-110bn in the Q4 guidance). We expect Norges Bank to issue the maximum amount, implying NOK 3bn in one of the 5 remaining auctions and NOK 2bn for the remaining auctions.
Supply 2027: The government’s budget proposal for 2027 showed an underlying borrowing requirement of NOK 93.6bn vs. 95.7bn in 2026. After years of under-borrowing, Norges Bank’s supply estimate has exceeded the underlying borrowing requirement over the past two years, with the aim of building up the cash reserves. We expect this to be the case also in 2027, implying a minimum of NOK 110bn in gross supply. The government’s borrowing mandate in long-term debt is increased by NOK 50bn to NOK 200bn, to provide greater flexibility and allowing for a potential increase in its own holdings. Risks to our supply estimate are thus skewed to the upside. Details will be provided in Norges Bank’s Strategy and borrowing programme due in December.

articles.title: French unrest weighs on Europe
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
French interest rate rises after turbulent weekend.
 This weekend's massive demonstrations, with between 500,000 and 800,000 participants in protests against deteriorating study conditions and high living costs, have resulted in fires, looting and other vandalism. French Interior Minister Nuñez takes responsibility for the riots and wants to resign, but President Macron has rejected his request. Curfews have been imposed in several cities.
The market reactions were reflected in sharp French interest rate rises yesterday, from already elevated levels. The ten-year government bond yield rose by almost 15 basis points to a high of 4.94% and the spread against the German ten-year widened. The European stock market index Euro Stoxx 50 fell by 1% and the Paris Stock Exchange marginally more, -1.1%. The weekend's protests have further intensified concerns about French public finances given the size of the austerity measures needed to significantly reduce the budget deficit.
In the US
, on the other hand, stock markets (S&P 500 +0.4% and Nasdaq +1.1%) rose, supported by a recovery in US technology stocks. However, high financing costs and uncertainty about the return on the large AI investments are likely to continue to affect the market. Oil traded erratically as the market weighed supply
risks in the Middle East against US easing of sanctions on Russian energy. US long-term interest rates rose slightly.
Asian stock markets are falling this morning. Futures point to positive and negative openings in the US and Europe today.
Preliminary results indicate that three quarters of Albertans wish the province to remain a part of Canada.
New tensions between the US and the EU?
 Over the weekend, Ukrainian President Zelenskyy stated that Elon Musk's Starlink, which the Ukrainian army uses to control its drones, does not allow drones to be connected if they are going faster than 160 km/h. This makes it difficult for Ukraine to shoot down Russian attack drones. Musk claims that President Trump has requested to reduce Starlink's capabilities while the White House says the opposite. Regardless of who made the decision, Ukraine is weakened while the Russian negotiating position is strengthened, and Zelenskyy has not held back with his criticism. The development paves the way for renewed strain between the EU and the United States.
Trump confirmed yesterday that he is open to a meeting between him, Chinese President Xi and Russian President Putin in mid-November and that the focus could be on Ukraine, nuclear weapons and trade. Ukraine's Zelenskyy said that a meeting between the US and Ukraine could take place in Norway within the next few days.
Today's most interesting data release
 is German producer prices
 for September, which will be important for assessing the inflationary effects of the conflict in the Middle East. So far, rising fuel, gas and electricity prices have been the driving force behind the rise in producer prices. At the same time, the price increases for input goods have slowed down at a monthly pace, but we will see if this year's energy shock breaks that trend.
Nordic key stories
Exploratory assignment to the Swedish Center Party leader. 
 Yesterday, Speaker of the Riksdag Andreas Norlén gave Center Party leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist the task of trying to form a government
. 
 According to Norlén, it is about Thand Ringqvist investigating the conditions for an alternative in the centre. It has been 37 days since the election and this will be the third exploratory assignment. Thand Ringqvist must report back to the Speaker no later than Monday 26 October.

articles.title: Fransk oro tynger Europa
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Franska ränteuppgångar efter orolig helg.
 Helgens massiva demonstrationer, med mellan 500 000 och 800 000 deltagare i protester mot försämrade studievillkor och höga levnadskostnader, har resulterat i bränder, plundringar och annan skadegörelse. Frankrikes inrikesminister Nuñez tar på sig en stor del av ansvaret för upploppen och vill avgå, men president Macron har avslagit hans begäran. Utegångsförbud har införts i flera städer.
Marknadsreaktionerna tog sig uttryck i kraftiga franska ränteuppgångar igår, från redan förhöjda nivåer. Den tioåriga statslåneräntan steg med nästan 15 räntepunkter till som mest 4,94% och differensen mot den tyska tioåringen ökade. Det europeiska börsindexet Euro Stoxx 50 föll med 1% och Parisbörsen marginellt mer, -1,1%. Helgens protester har ytterligare förstärkt oron över de franska statsfinanserna med tanke på storleken på de åtstramningar som behövs för att märkbart minska budgetunderskottet.
I USA
 steg däremot börserna (S&P 500 +0,4% och Nasdaq +1,1%) med stöd av en återhämtning i amerikanska teknikaktier. Höga finansieringskostnader och osäkerhet kring avkastningen på de stora AI-investeringarna lär dock fortsätta påverka marknaden. Oljan handlades ryckigt då marknaden vägde in
utbudsrisker i Mellanöstern mot amerikanska lättnader i sanktionerna mot rysk energi. Amerikanska långräntor steg något.
Asiatiska börser faller nu på morgonen. Terminerna pekar på positiva respektive negativa öppningar i USA och Europa idag.
I skrivande stund finns ännu inga valresultat efter gårdagens folkomröstning i den kanadensiska provinsen Alberta om självständighet.
Nya spänningar mellan USA och EU?
 Under helgen uppgav Ukrainas president Zelenskyj att Elon Musks Starlink, som ukrainska armén använder för att styra sina drönare, inte låter drönare vara uppkopplade om de åker snabbare än 160 km/h. Detta försvårar för Ukraina att skjuta ner ryska attackdrönare. Musk hävdar att president Trump har begärt att reducera Starlinks kapacitet medan Vita huset säger det motsatta. Oavsett vem som tagit beslutet försvagas Ukraina medan det ryska förhandlingsläget stärks, och Zelenskyj har inte hållit igen med sin kritik. Utvecklingen bäddar för nya motsättningar mellan EU och USA.
Trump bekräftade igår att han är öppen för ett möte mellan honom, Kinas president Xi och Rysslands president Putin i mitten av november och att fokus kan vara Ukraina, kärnvapen och handel. Ukrainas Zelenskyj sa att ett möte mellan USA och Ukraina kan komma att äga rum i Norge inom de närmaste dagarna.
Dagens mest intressanta datasläpp
 är tyska producentpriser
 för september som blir viktiga för att bedöma inflationseffekterna av konflikten i Mellanöstern. Hittills har stigande bränsle-, gas- och elpriser varit drivande i uppgången i producentpriserna. Samtidigt har prisökningarna på insatsvaror i månadstakt bromsat in men vi får se om årets energichock bryter den trenden.
Sverige
Sonderingsuppdrag till centerledaren. 
Riksdagens talman Andreas Norlén gav igår Centerpartiets ledare Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist i uppdrag att försöka bilda regering
. 
Enligt Norlén handlar det om att Thand Ringqvist ska undersöka förutsättningarna för ett mittenalternativ. Det har gått 37 dagar sedan valet och detta blir det tredje sonderingsuppdraget. Thand Ringqvist ska rapportera tillbaka till talmannen senast måndagen 26 oktober.

articles.title: DGB'35 & DGB'52
articles.heading: DGB Auction Preview
articles.fulltext:
Wednesday, October 21, 2026, 
Nationalbanken
 will offer 
10Y 2.25% DGB 2035 (992496) and 
30Y 0.25% DGB 2052 (992402). 
Bids can be submitted as from the opening of MTS Denmark until 10.15 CET.
General: 
Wednesday 
Nationalbanken
 will offer DGB’35 and DGB’52 at the auction.
Target for DGB issuance is set at DKK 65 bn in 2026, which is unchanged compared to 2022-2025.
Prior to Wednesday’s auction YTD issuance amounts to 81.8% of the annual target.
Current implied FX EURDKK-hedge provides a pickup of 44.1 bps pa. in 3M vs. EGBs.
DGB’35:
DGB’35 trades at -16.3 bps vs the German curve which is 0.2 bps wider than at the last auction on October 7. 
DGB’35 has widened 0.5 bps vs DESTR since the last auction to 17.1 bps. 
The YTM roll from DGB’35 to DGB’33 is 12.5 bps which is 3.3 bps tighter than at the last auction. 
The 10Y FX hedged excess yield in DGB vs. core EGBs is now 26.1 bps vs. Germany which is 1.6 bps wider than at the last auction, and 17.2 bps vs. the Netherlands which is 3.4 bps wider than at the last auction.
DGB’35 has -0.9 bps in ASW-pickup (vs. 3M Euribor) vs. DBR Aug-35 which is 0.2 bps wider than at the last auction.
DGB’35 new issuance premium is 5.6 bps vs Germany, which is 0.3 bps wider than the last auction, and 2.8 bps vs DESTR which is 0.2 bps tighter than at the last auction.
We see current pricing of DGB’35 as fair to expensive
DGB’52: 
Unlike usual there is no maximal nominal sale indicated (usually 1.5-2 bn).
DGB’52 trades at -41.0 bps vs the German curve which is 0.5 bps wider than at the last auction.
DGB’52 trades at 27.6 bps vs DESTR, which is 0.2 bps wider than at the last auction.
DGB’52 has -30.5 bps 
in ASW-pickup (vs. 3M Euribor)
 vs DBR 08/52, which is 0.6 bps wider than at the last auction.
We see current pricing of DGB’52 as expensive.

articles.title: Rebound in risk appetite despite war and riots
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
The US stock markets fell back on Friday 
and the S&P 500 closed just over 1% lower and the Nasdaq just over 2% lower. More and more analysts are warning of unrealistic expectations and difficult to understand financing of large AI investments. The Nasdaq has fallen by 5% since its peak in early October, but the decline is still small compared to the sharp rise in recent years. Risk appetite has, however, recovered somewhat this morning. Developments in Asia are mixed, while US futures are rising. Futures in Europe, however, are pointing slightly downwards.
The reporting season kicks off 
in earnest this week with quarterly reports from a wide range of international and Swedish companies. SpaceX, Meta and Tesla will present quarterly results during the week and on Thursday SEB will publish its report. It remains to be seen whether the generally high expectations 
for interim reports 
can be met.
The wars around the Persian Gulf and in Ukraine, along with the riots in France 
that have also spread to Italy, among others, continue to dominate the news flow. Oil prices rose to almost $110 per barrel (Brent) on Friday. Trump's agreement to buy diesel from Russia has so far had no noticeable effect on prices, while Ukraine continues to defy Trump by attacking Russian energy facilities. 
Trump has also decided to pause the so-called Graham Act for 60 days, i.e. the planned package of sanctions against Russia that Congress approved a couple of weeks ago.
 Putin is reportedly trying to bring about peace talks with China and the United States, without Ukrainian participation. Despite that, oil prices are falling by a couple of dollars this morning.
In Canada, the province of Alberta is voting
 on independence today. A strong result for the separatists could put pressure on Prime Minister Carney, although the probability of a separatist victory is very low, according to Polymarket.
After rising to a new record level in the wake of last week's unexpectedly high inflation, the US ten-year yield fell quickly by around 25 basis points.
 However, no real momentum in the decline has materialised and US yields closed largely unchanged on Friday after a volatile trading day.
It is a relatively thin week on the data front, 
but it will be interesting to see if the PMI in the euro area and the US continues to rise or if the upturn stops, in line with consensus forecasts. Price expectations will be particularly interesting to study after the recent sharp rises in energy prices. British inflation is expected to rise. The Fed has entered its quiet period ahead of the interest rate announcement on 28 October. After large swings in expectations, the market now seems to have landed on the fact that the interest rate is likely to be left unchanged. The probability of a hike in October has dropped to around 15%. GDP in China presented overnight rose by 1.2%, 4.5% y/y in the third quarter, which was slightly stronger than expected.
Nordic key stories
No statistics from Sweden this week, but on Thursday the National Mediation Office will hold a conference on the conditions for the 2027 wage negotiations, 
where Deputy Governor Per Jansson will give the Riksbank's view of the situation in a speech. In the coming weeks, the Swedish Confederation of Trade Unions (LO) is expected to present the trade unions' demands ahead of the negotiations. Ahead of the 2025 collective bargaining round, the union's demands were 4.2%, which was presented on 4 November. The demands are usually a good indicator of where the agreements will end up. On average, the LO has got about 75% of the original demands through. The employers argue on DN Debatt today that the rate of wage increases needs to slow down, and against the ideas of a shortening of working hours
(Swedish payment link 
here
)
The Speaker of the Riksdag will hold a press conference at 1:00 p.m 
. today to present the next step in the formation of a government. Most political experts are inclined to believe that Ulf Kristersson (Moderates) will be given the task of probing the conditions for a new government, but relatively many believe that it could instead be Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist (Center party). It is difficult to know what is being said behind closed doors, but the tactic seems to be to let the opponents fail in the first prime ministerial votes and then try to push through their own line in the decisive fourth vote. Then the choice can be between abandoning their red lines or going to a special election. The question is what happens if several parties use the same tactics, especially if the negotiations leading up to the votes are mainly about who should sit in the government rather than what policies should be pursued. The Sweden Democrats' open letter to the Center Party, with the aim of persuading the party to change sides, seems to have little chance of success, at least for the time being.

articles.title: Rekyl i riskaptiten trots krig och upplopp
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
De amerikanska börserna föll tillbaka i fredags 
och S&P 500 stängde drygt 1% lägre och Nasdaq drygt 2% lägre. Allt fler varnar för orealistiska förväntningar och svårgenomskådlig finansiering av stora AI-investeringar. Nasdaq har visserligen fallit med 5% sedan toppen i början av oktober, men nedgången är fortfarande liten jämfört med de senaste årens kraftiga uppgång. Riskaptiten har dessutom återhämtat sig något nu på morgonen. Utvecklingen i Asien är blandad, samtidigt som USA-terminerna stiger. Terminerna i Europa pekar dock svagt nedåt.
Rapportsäsongen tar fart 
på allvar denna vecka med kvartalsrapporter från en lång rad internationella och svenska företag. SpaceX, Meta och Tesla presenterar kvartalsresultat under veckan och på torsdag kommer SEB med sin rapport. Det återstår att se om de högt ställda förväntningarna 
på delårsrapporter
na kan infrias.
Krigen kring Persiska viken och i Ukraina, tillsammans med upploppen i Frankrike 
som även har spridit sig till bl a Italien, fortsätter att dominera nyhetsflödet. Oljepriset steg till nästan 110 dollar per fat (Brent) i fredags. Trumps avtal om att köpa diesel från Ryssland har hittills inte haft någon märkbar effekt på priserna, samtidigt som Ukraina fortsätter att trotsa Trump genom att angripa ryska energianläggningar. 
Trump har även beslutat att pausa den s k Graham-lagen i 60 dagar, d v s det planerade sanktionspaketet mot Ryssland som kongressen godkänt för ett par veckor sedan.
 Putin uppges försöka få till stånd fredssamtal med Kina och USA, utan ukrainskt deltagande. Trots det faller oljepriset med ett par dollar nu på morgonen.
I Kanada röstar provinsen Alberta
 om självständighet i dag. Ett starkt resultat för separatisterna kan sätta press på premiärminister Carney, även om sannolikheten för en separatistisk seger är mycket låg enligt Polymarket.
Efter att ha stigit till en ny rekordnivå i spåren av förra veckans oväntat höga inflation föll den amerikanska tioårsräntan snabbt med omkring 25 räntepunkter.
 Något riktigt momentum i nedgången har dock inte infunnit sig och de amerikanska räntorna stängde i stort sett oförändrade i fredags efter en svängig handelsdag.
Det är en relativt tunn vecka på datafronten, 
men det blir intressant att se om PMI i euroområdet och USA fortsätter att stiga eller om uppgången stannar av, i linje med konsensusprognoserna. Prisförväntningarna blir särskilt intressanta att studera efter de senaste kraftiga uppgångarna i energipriserna. Den brittiska inflationen väntas stiga. Fed har gått in i sin tysta period inför räntebeskedet den 28 oktober. Efter stora svängningar i förväntningarna tycks marknaden nu ha landat i att räntan sannolikt lämnas oförändrad. Sannolikheten för en höjning i oktober har sjunkit till omkring 15%. BNP i Kina som presenterats under natten steg med 1,2%, 4,5% år/år under tredje kvartalet vilket var lite starkare än väntat.
Sverige
Ingen statistik från Sverige denna vecka, men på torsdag håller Medlingsinstitutet en konferens om förutsättningarna inför lönerörelsen 2027, 
där vice riksbankschef Per Jansson i ett tal kommer att ge Riksbankens syn på läget. LO väntas under de närmaste veckorna presentera fackförbundens krav inför förhandlingarna. Inför avtalsrörelsen 2025 låg industrins krav på 4,2%, vilket presenterades den 4 november. Kraven brukar vara en bra indikator på var avtalen till slut hamnar. I genomsnitt har LO fått igenom omkring 75% av de ursprungliga kraven. Arbetsgivarna argumenterar på DN Debatt i dag för att löneökningstakten behöver bromsa in, och emot idéerna om en förkortning av arbetstiden
(betallänk 
här
)
Riksdagens talman håller presskonferens klockan 13.00 
i dag för att presentera nästa steg i regeringsbildningen. De flesta politiska experter lutar åt att Ulf Kristersson (M) får uppdraget att sondera förutsättningarna för en ny regering, men relativt många tror att det i stället kan bli Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist (C). Det är svårt att veta vad som sägs bakom stängda dörrar, men taktiken tycks vara att låta motståndarna misslyckas i de första statsministeromröstningarna för att sedan försöka driva igenom sin egen linje i den avgörande fjärde omröstningen. Då kan valet stå mellan att överge sina röda linjer eller att gå till extraval. Frågan är vad som händer om flera partier använder samma taktik, särskilt om förhandlingarna fram till omröstningarna främst handlar om vilka som ska sitta i regeringen snarare än vilken politik som ska föras. Sverigedemokraternas öppna brev till Centern, med syftet att förmå partiet att byta sida, verkar i alla fall i nuläget ha små möjligheter att lyckas.

articles.title: Calm data week ahead with PMIs in focus
articles.heading: The Week Ahead
articles.fulltext:
Euro area and US PMIs take centre stage in an otherwise quiet week for economic data. In the US, the Fed’s pre-meeting blackout period begins tomorrow, but markets will remain focused on the upcoming Fed decision and US midterm elections. In Norway, manufacturing sentiment and unemployment data will be in focus, while Sweden has a quiet data calendar. The week will also bring several interesting Q3 reports, including SEB’s on Thursday.
US:
No major data releases. September PMIs will be watched for signs of continued strong economic momentum. We will also get housing data. Otherwise, the run-up to the Fed’s 28 October decision and the 3 November midterm elections will be in focus.
Euro area: 
Flash PMI for October will be the main event. French business confidence (INSEE), German producer prices and euro area inflation expectations will also be worth watching for further insights into economic activity and inflationary pressures. 
Sweden:
No economic indicators this week. At 13:00 on Monday, the speaker of parliament is expected to announce the next step in the process to form a new government. The Riksbank’s Jansson will speak on Thursday at the Mediation Office conference on the economic conditions for wage formation. 
Norway:
 This week offers input from the manufacturing sector, and we will see if the minor optimism in Q2 was a one-off or the beginning of a new trend. Weak demand in both the domestic and export market is weighing on manufacturing, but sentiment is nevertheless pointing to increased production ahead. The LFS unemployment rate, due Wednesday, has edged marginally lower from the beginning of the year due to increased employment among young workers. Excluding young workers, the LFS unemployment rate has been broadly stable.
